header: A photoresist is a polymeric material sensitive to light of specific wavelengths. Upon irradiation, it undergoes specific chemical reactions that substantially change its solubility in a developer, thereby forming the desired pattern on the surface of a semiconductor material. As a key patterning material in integrated-circuit fabrication, advances in photoresist chemistry directly determine the limits of process miniaturization and the industry's capacity for technological self-reliance.

subquestions.text_open:
3.1 The novolak-diazonaphthoquinone (Novolak-DNQ) system is the most widely used photoresist for the g-line (436 nm) and i-line (365 nm). One component is a high-molecular-weight linear phenolic resin, and the other is diazonaphthoquinone, whose structure is shown below.
3.1.1 The phenolic resin prepared under acidic conditions is a low-molecular-weight linear prepolymer. The curing agent hexamethylenetetramine may be added to an aqueous solution of the prepolymer to cure and cross-link it upon heating. Identify which substrate must be used in excess when preparing the acid-catalyzed phenolic resin, write the decomposition equation of the curing agent upon heating, and on this basis state the role of the curing agent.
3.1.2 State the principal intermolecular forces between the two components of the Novolak-DNQ system.

3.1.3 In the Novolak-DNQ system, the photosensitive component undergoes rearrangement upon irradiation to form unstable structure A, which then forms B in the alkaline developer N(CH_3)_4^+OH^-, changing the solubility of the photoresist. Write the SMILES representations of A and B.

3.2 PVCi is a high-resolution photoresist. One method for synthesizing PVCi is shown below.
3.2.1 The first step is a conventional free-radical polymerization of a double bond, and all subsequent steps are functional-group substitutions. Write the SMILES representations of X, Y, Z, and PVCi. The terminal-group structures need not be specified; use [*] to denote the connection sites at the two ends of the polymer backbone.

text_images.description: X (C_4H_6O_2) reacts under AIBN/CH_3OH conditions to give Y; Y reacts under CH_3OH/NaOH conditions to give Z; Z reacts with 'O=C(Cl)/C=C/C1=CC=CC=C1' to give PVCi.

subquestions.text_open: 3.2.2 Write the SMILES representation of the structure formed by the interchain reaction of PVCi upon irradiation at 360 nm. The terminal-group structures and degrees of polymerization need not be specified; use [*] and [**] to denote connection sites in the polymer chains.
